rule_1_14_message: Primary amine group reacts with the aldehyde (reducing) group of sugar. In the presence of moisture, this causes browning of the blend, formation of toxic adducts, and loss of API activity.
rule_1_14_suggestion: Replace the reducing sugar with inert one (Sucrose), Mannitol, or MCC.
rule_1_9_message: Alkaline salts (Stearates) create a local alkaline microenvironment, accelerating hydrolytic cleavage of amines in a moist environment.
rule_1_9_suggestion: Replace magnesium stearate with stearic acid or PRUV (SSF).
rule_1_10_message: Carbonates and other alkaline inorganic salts degrade primary amines.
rule_6_9_message: Aliphatic organic acid reacts with alkaline lubricant, disrupting the lubricating grid of the stearate.
rule_6_9_suggestion: Use an acidic or neutral lubricant.
rule_7_9_message: Aromatic organic acid reacts with alkaline lubricant, disrupting the lubricating grid of the stearate.
rule_7_9_suggestion: Use an acidic or neutral lubricant.
rule_6_10_message: Organic acids react with carbonates releasing carbon dioxide in a moist environment, which will lead to swelling and destruction of the tablet.
rule_6_10_suggestion: Avoid carbonates unless it is an effervescent tablet.
rule_21_19_message: Phenolic groups are capable of forming hydrogen bonds with polymer chains (PVP, PEG), which may delay dissolution in vitro.
rule_21_19_suggestion: Check dissolution kinetics; it may be necessary to increase the disintegrant share.
rule_23_9_message: Fat-soluble vitamins are extremely sensitive to the alkaline environment of stearates.
rule_23_10_message: Fat-soluble vitamins oxidize in the alkaline environment of inorganic salts.
rule_23_28_message: Trace amounts of heavy metals in silicates (Talc) catalyze vitamin oxidation.
rule_23_28_suggestion: Avoid talc or use chelating agents (EDTA).
rule_23_13_message: Calcium ions and trace metals in phosphates catalyze vitamin degradation.
rule_6_13_message: Divalent calcium ions in the phosphate catalyze the oxidation of aliphatic organic acids (e.g. Vitamin C).
rule_7_13_message: Interaction of an aromatic organic acid with a calcium salt forms poorly soluble complexes, reducing bioavailability.
rule_26_13_message: Fatty acids (Stearic acid) form insoluble calcium salts upon contact with phosphates.
rule_1_17_message: Polyols (Sorbitol) may contain trace amounts of reducing sugars that react with primary amines.
rule_27_9_message: Proteins and enzymes are prone to alkaline hydrolysis in the presence of alkaline salts.
